::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 13th [1869]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Columbia University Library, New York: Lohf Collection
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd),

I hope you and the Incurable List are safe together somewhere![^1] I had no list of my own so I asked a friend to send you hers, and owing to some blundering of mine I really do not know whether she sent it to Wilden manor or to Charlton.

Will you kindly when you have looked it over return it addressed

[Miss Jacob](people/person_749.qmd)
Crawley Rectory
Winchester

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: The 'incurable list' was evidently a list of candidates for admission to an asylum;  perhaps either the [Home for Incurable and Infirm Women](organizations/other_26.qmd) or the [Royal Hospital for Incurables](organizations/other_37.qmd).
